Hi Ethan — great chat today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a few asks so we can move your Private VPC evaluation forward.

Recap (from our call)
- You prefer a private networking option for production (data residency + egress control).
- Primary options we discussed: PrivateLink (private endpoint) vs VPC Peering (direct VPC-to-VPC).
- You’re evaluating throughput needs now; initial usage looks like 10–20 req/s with spikes to ~150 req/s.

Immediate asks so our infra team can validate:
1) Preferred connectivity mode (PrivateLink or Peering) — if undecided, tell us which is higher priority: firewall simplicity or raw throughput.
2) Egress/ingress IPs or CIDR(s) we should expect from your side (for allowlist).
3) Any mandatory network controls: mutual TLS, mTLS cert rotation cadence, IPsec, or enforced proxy egress.
4) Target go-live window (approx).

Attachments: I’ve attached our network requirements doc (redwood_network_requirements_v1.pdf) which lists ports and recommended NAT/allowlist entries.

Next steps we recommend after you return answers above:
- We’ll have NetEng scope the PrivateLink endpoint (if chosen) and return a minimal list of IPs and ports for your firewall team.
- If you prefer Peering for throughput, we’ll prepare a brief peering runbook and estimated provisioning ETA.

Thanks — can you share the CIDR(s) and confirm whether PrivateLink is acceptable? If you want, loop in your infra lead and I’ll include our network engineer.

Best,

4) Target go-live: aiming for a pilot in mid-May (week of May 17).

I attached our high-level topology (novatrade_network_topology_v1.pdf). A few clarifying questions:

Thanks for the flag — reviewed topology and customer requirements. High-level guidance below (keeps it short so sales can share with the customer):

Option A — PrivateLink (recommended for pilot)
- mTLS: Supported. We host the PrivateLink endpoint in the Redwood account; we support TLS termination that can require client certs. Customer can upload client certs via our Console (or we can accept a signed CA bundle for validation). Rotation: we support rolling cert swaps with a brief overlap window to avoid downtime; quarterly rotation is fine.
- Egress IPs: For the data plane (actual inference traffic) there are no additional Redwood egress IPs that require allowlisting beyond the endpoint network interface in the PrivateLink VPC. For health checks/control-plane callbacks we will need to be allowed to reach your endpoint on TCP/443 from the following minimum control IPs: 203.0.113.10, 203.0.113.11 (these are our control-plane NAT addresses).
- Throughput: PrivateLink will comfortably handle the pilot numbers (10–20 req/s, spikes to 150 s) but if you expect sustained high concurrency (1k+ concurrent calls) we should discuss Dedicated capacity.
- Ports/timeouts: TCP/443 only; idle timeout 350s recommended for streaming calls.

Option B — VPC Peering (recommended if you need the absolute lowest latency and very high sustained throughput)
- Peering removes the need for Public/PrivateLink endpoints but adds cross-account networking governance. Provisioning ETA: 3–5 business days after receiving your VPC ID and CIDR confirmation (we’ll prepare a peering request and a security group/route table plan).
- We’ll provide a peering runbook and required IAM/route changes.

Next technical asks for the customer to finalize:
- Confirm whether NovaTrade can accept our listed control-plane IPs 203.0.113.10/11 for health checks.
- Confirm the exact CIDR (you mentioned 10.12.0.0/24, please confirm whether that will be the source range for traffic).
- If you choose PrivateLink, have your security team prepare the client cert or CA bundle for us to validate.

I’m copying this into our internal ticket: ENG-REQ-9321 and will follow-up with a short tech note. If they want, I can schedule a 30-min NetEng call early next week.

Ben Carter
